question: Queue item 20261030-1251-expand-dev-services-c696-u04-q03: should the interface vocabulary get oidc and mcp terms? Proposal: oidc for a service reached as an OAuth 2.0 authorization server and OpenID Connect provider through its discovery document and its authorization, token and userinfo endpoints (dev-services/auth0: the Authentication API; dev-services/clerk: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, /oauth/token and /oauth/userinfo; dev-services/stytch: the Connected Apps OpenID configuration endpoint; dev-services/workos: WorkOS Connect, /.well-known/openid-configuration and /oauth2/userinfo), and mcp for a Model Context Protocol server that an AI tool reaches at a server URL (dev-services/growthbook: hosted at https://mcp.growthbook.io/mcp with OAuth sign-in on GrowthBook Cloud). Each of the five records keeps rest and names the protocol in interface_detail.
why: Neither protocol has an interface term. The mcp term is also asked for by queue items 20261030-1251-expand-dev-services-c696-u01-q03 (Honeycomb, UptimeRobot) and 20261030-1251-expand-dev-services-c696-u02-q01 (Zapier, Pipedream), so one change can serve all. WorkOS also documents AuthKit as an OAuth authorization server for MCP servers (workos.com/docs/reference/workos-connect/metadata), which is not an MCP server of its own. The Auth0 Authentication API page names SAML and FAPI beside OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0, and Clerk, Stytch and WorkOS sell SAML single sign-on and SCIM; whether saml and scim need terms is a separate decision.
